```{r}
# Function to subset the columns for the preparation of Mutation ID 
prepare_structure_mut_id_columns <- function(df, chain_name = "1") {
  filtered <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(aa_mut_class) & aa_mut_class != "Synonymous",
      !is.na(aa_mut_wt) & aa_mut_wt != "*",
      !is.na(aa_mut_sub) & aa_mut_sub != "*",
      !is.na(aa_mut_pos)
    )

  message("Filtered rows: ", nrow(filtered))
  
  result <- filtered %>%
    mutate(
      
      aa_mut_id    = paste0(aa_mut_wt, aa_mut_pos, aa_mut_sub),
      ddmut_mut_id = paste(chain_name, aa_mut_id)
    )

  message("Final rows: ", nrow(result))
  return(result)
}
```

### 2) Load and process Predictions
RSA data process
```{r}
# Function to calculate Spearman correlation per gene x RSASA baselines
compute_rsasa_performance <- function(
  df,
  predictors,
  gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
  response_col
) {

  #library(dplyr)
  #library(purrr)
  #library(tibble)

  # ---- helper: map predictor to clean name ----
  get_predictor_name <- function(pred) {
    case_when(
      pred %in% c("RSASA_complex", "dRSASA_complex") ~ "RSA (complex)",
      pred %in% c("RSASA_monomer", "RSASA_monomer_rescaled") ~ "RSA (monomer)",
      TRUE ~ pred
    )
  }

  df %>%
    group_split(.data[[gene_col]]) %>%
    map_dfr(function(df_gene) {

      gene_name <- unique(df_gene[[gene_col]])

      map_dfr(predictors, function(pred) {

        predictor_name <- get_predictor_name(pred)
        predictor_input_modality <- "RSA Baselines"

        # ---- missing predictor ----
        if (!pred %in% names(df_gene)) {
          return(tibble(
            gene_name = gene_name,
            predictor_name = predictor_name,
            predictor_input_modality = predictor_input_modality,
            model_type = "Spearman",
            metric = c("Spearman_r", "Spearman_p", "Spearman_R2"),
            value = NA_real_
          ))
        }

        x <- df_gene[[pred]]
        y <- df_gene[[response_col]]

        keep <- !(is.na(x) | is.na(y))
        x <- x[keep]
        y <- y[keep]

        # ---- insufficient data ----
        if (length(x) < 2 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
          return(tibble(
            gene_name = gene_name,
            predictor_name = predictor_name,
            predictor_input_modality = predictor_input_modality,
            model_type = "Spearman",
            metric = c("Spearman_r", "Spearman_p", "Spearman_R2"),
            value = NA_real_
          ))
        }

        # ---- compute correlation ----
        sp <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman"))

        tibble(
          gene_name = gene_name,
          predictor_name = predictor_name,
          predictor_input_modality = predictor_input_modality,
          model_type = "Spearman",
          metric = c("Spearman_r", "Spearman_p", "Spearman_R2"),
          value = c(
            unname(sp$estimate),
            sp$p.value,
            unname(sp$estimate)^2
          )
        )
      })
    })
}


# Function to run Spearman Correlation cleanly
# 1) the minimal version to calcualte spearman correlation
compute_spearman_by_gene <- function(
  df,
  predictor_col,
  fitness_col,
  group_cols = "aa_mut_gene",
  min_score = NULL
) {

  library(dplyr)

  # ---- Check predictor exists ----
  if (!predictor_col %in% names(df)) {
    stop(paste("Predictor column not found:", predictor_col))
  }

  # ---- Filter NA ----
  df <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[predictor_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[fitness_col]])
    )

  # ---- Optional threshold ----
  if (!is.null(min_score)) {
    df <- df %>%
      filter(.data[[predictor_col]] > min_score)
  }

  # ---- Compute correlations ----
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),

      r = {
        x <- .data[[predictor_col]]
        y <- .data[[fitness_col]]

        if (length(x) < 3 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman"))
        }
      },

      R2 = r^2,

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# 2) a robust version to handle control when group_cols = NULL
compute_spearman_by_gene <- function(
  df,
  predictor_col,
  fitness_col,
  group_cols = "aa_mut_gene",
  min_score = NULL
) {

  library(dplyr)

  # ---- Check predictor exists ----
  if (!predictor_col %in% names(df)) {
    stop(paste("Predictor column not found:", predictor_col))
  }

  # ---- Filter NA ----
  df <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[predictor_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[fitness_col]])
    )

  # ---- Optional threshold ----
  if (!is.null(min_score)) {
    df <- df %>%
      filter(.data[[predictor_col]] > min_score)
  }

  # ---- Handle empty data ----
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(n = NA, r = NA, R2 = NA))
  }

  # =====================================================
  # CASE 1: NO grouping (technical control)
  # =====================================================
  if (is.null(group_cols)) {

    x <- df[[predictor_col]]
    y <- df[[fitness_col]]

    r <- if (length(x) < 3 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman"))
    }

    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        n = nrow(df),
        r = r,
        R2 = r^2
      )
    )
  }

  # =====================================================
  # CASE 2: GROUPED (ΦX / ProteinGym)
  # =====================================================
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),

      r = {
        x <- .data[[predictor_col]]
        y <- .data[[fitness_col]]

        if (length(x) < 3 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman"))
        }
      },

      R2 = r^2,

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}


# Function to transform to long format
transform_corr_results <- function(
  df,
  gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
  gene_name_col = "gene_name"
) {

  # ---- detect available metrics ----
  metric_cols <- intersect(c("r", "R2", "p"), colnames(df))

  df %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("n")) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(!!gene_name_col := dplyr::all_of(gene_col)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::all_of(metric_cols),
      names_to = "metric",
      values_to = "value"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      metric = dplyr::recode(
        metric,
        r  = "Spearman_r",
        R2 = "Spearman_R2",
        p  = "Spearman_p"
      ),
      model_type = "Spearman"
    )
}
```

Process prediction results
- correct aa positions for proteins F and J
```{r}
# Function to shift aa positions in mut id
shift_mutant_position <- function(
  df,
  mutant_col,
  new_col = "aa_mut_id",
  shift = 1
) {

  df[[new_col]] <- stringr::str_replace(
    df[[mutant_col]],
    "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])",
    ~ paste0(
        stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")[,2],
        as.integer(stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")[,3]) + shift,
        stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")[,4]
      )
  )

  df
}

# Function to shift specific positions
shift_specific_mutant_position <- function(
  df,
  mutant_col,
  new_col = "aa_mut_id",
  shift = 1,
  pos_min = -Inf,
  pos_max = Inf
) {

  df[[new_col]] <- stringr::str_replace(
    df[[mutant_col]],
    "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])",
    ~ {
      m <- stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")
      wt  <- m[,2]
      pos <- as.integer(m[,3])
      sub <- m[,4]

      pos_new <- ifelse(
        pos >= pos_min & pos <= pos_max,
        pos + shift,
        pos
      )

      paste0(wt, pos_new, sub)
    }
  )

  df
}
```

## Prepare Proteins Data
1) Prepare protein data match PDB files
2) Remove the aa positions lost structural information and were not in PDB;

    1) D1: 1,2,3,4,5,149,150,151,152 (6-148)

    3) D3: 1,2,3,4,145,146,147,148,149,150,151,152 (5-144)

## MSA data 
### 1) MSA statistics
Load EVcouplings MSA results from: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23889160
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(fs)

# define the root directory
#msa_root <- "./data/EVcoupling_MSA"


# find all statistics files
msa_stat_files <- dir_ls(
  path = msa_root,
  recurse = TRUE,
  regexp = "_alignment_statistics\\.csv$"
)

length(msa_stat_files)


# read and parse
msa_alignment_statistics <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    msa_stat_files,
    function(file){

      # read statistics file
      df <- read.csv(
        file,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )

      path_parts <-
        strsplit(
          normalizePath(file),
          .Platform$file.sep
        )[[1]]

      # database
      database <-
        path_parts[
          grepl(
            "^EVcouplings_MSA_a2m",
            path_parts
          )
        ][1]
      
      database <-
        sub(
          "^EVcouplings_MSA_a2m_",
          "",
          database
        )
      # protein
      protein_folder <-
        path_parts[
          grepl(
            "_EVcouplings_MSA_a2m$",
            path_parts
          )
        ][1]
      
      protein <-
        sub(
          "_EVcouplings_MSA_a2m$",
          "",
          protein_folder
        )
      
      # bitscore
      align_idx <-
        which(path_parts == "align")
      
      bitscore_folder <-
        path_parts[align_idx - 1]
      
      bitscore <-
        sub(
          "^TARGET_b",
          "",
          bitscore_folder
        )

      # hash folder
      hash_folder_index <-
        which(path_parts == protein_folder) + 1

      hash_folder <-
        path_parts[
          hash_folder_index
        ]

      df %>%
        mutate(
          database = database,
          protein = protein,
          bitscore = bitscore,
          hash_folder = hash_folder,
          statistics_file = file
        )
    }
  )


# check loaded data 
msa_alignment_statistics %>%
  select(
    database,
    protein,
    bitscore,
    num_seqs,
    N_eff
  ) %>%
  head()




```



### 2) Statistics (Meff, Meff_L, Quality)
Load and plot the Meff (Meff/L) by proteins as the bitscores increase
```{r}
# load raw data
#phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw <- read_csv("./codes_Github_final/data/EVcouplings_MSA/phix_MSA_EVcouplings_results.csv")

# process raw data
head(as.data.frame(phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw), 5)


# remove unused rows
phix_MSA_EVcouplings <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw %>%
  slice(-(1:2)) %>%
  mutate(dataset = str_extract(Jobs, "(?<=EVcouplings_).*")) 

 
# split results to Meff and Meff/L 
seq_cols <- grep("^Sequences", names(phix_MSA_EVcouplings), value = TRUE)
qual_cols <- grep("^Quality", names(phix_MSA_EVcouplings), value = TRUE)

bitscores <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)

for(i in seq_along(bitscores)) {
  
  seq_col  <- seq_cols[i]
  qual_col <- qual_cols[i]
  b        <- bitscores[i]
  
  phix_MSA_EVcouplings <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings %>%
    
    mutate(
      !!paste0("Meff_b", b) := as.numeric(
        str_extract(.data[[seq_col]], "^\\d+")
      ),
      
      !!paste0("Meff_L_b", b) := as.numeric(
        str_extract(.data[[seq_col]], "(?<=\\()[0-9.]+")
      ),
      
      !!paste0("quality_b", b) := as.numeric(.data[[qual_col]])
    )
}


# drop original result columns
phix_MSA_EVcouplings_clean <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings %>%
  select(
    Protein,
    Jobs,
    dataset,
    Download,
    starts_with("Meff_b"),
    starts_with("Meff_L_b"),
    starts_with("quality_b")
  ) %>%
  rename(
    protein = Protein,
    database = dataset
  )

# transform to long format
phix_MSA_EVcouplings_long <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(Meff|Meff_L|quality)_b"),
    names_to = c(".value", "bitscore"),
    names_pattern = "(Meff|Meff_L|quality)_b(.*)"
```

### 3) Single mutants matrix (from selected EVcouplings MSA)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 1. Load the single-mutant matrices only within the selected runs
# ============================================================

selected_output_dir <- "./codes_Github_final/data/EVcouplings_MSA/EVcoupling_MSA_selected"

# Load all 11 selected EVcouplings single-mutant matrices
selected_single_mutant_files <-
  dir_ls(
    selected_output_dir,
    recurse = TRUE,
    regexp = "_single_mutant_matrix\\.csv$"
  )

length(
  selected_single_mutant_files
)
# [1] 11

EVcouplings_single_mutant_matrix <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    selected_single_mutant_files,
    function(file) {

      path_parts <-
        strsplit(
          normalizePath(file),
          .Platform$file.sep
        )[[1]]

      # Identify selected protein folder
      protein_folder <-
        path_parts[
          grepl(
            "_EVcouplings_MSA_selected$",
            path_parts
          )
        ][1]

      # Extract protein name
      protein <-
        sub(
          "_EVcouplings_MSA_selected$",
          "",
          protein_folder
        )

      # Read matrix
      df <-
        read.csv(
          file,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )

      df %>%
        mutate(
          protein = protein,
          source_file = file
        )
    }
  )

# Adjust residue numbering with the DMS dataset
EVcouplings_single_mutant_matrix <-
  EVcouplings_single_mutant_matrix %>%

  mutate(

    # Original EVcouplings sequence position
    pos_sequence =
      as.integer(pos),

    # Analysis position used in the DMS dataset
    pos_analysis =
      case_when(
        protein %in% c("F", "J") ~
          pos_sequence - 1L,

        TRUE ~
          pos_sequence
      ),

    wt =
      as.character(wt),

    subs =
      as.character(subs),

    # Reconstruct mutation using corrected numbering
    mutant_analysis =
      paste0(
        wt,
        pos_analysis,
        subs
      ),

    # Same identifier used for predictor merging
    residue_mut_id =
      paste0(
        protein,
        "_",
        mutant_analysis
      )
  ) %>%

  # Remove position 0 generated by F/J shift
  filter(
    pos_analysis > 0
  )

EVcouplings_single_mutant_matrix %>%

    protein %in% c("F", "J")
  ) %>%
  select(
    protein,
    mutant,
    pos_sequence,
    pos_analysis,
    wt,
    subs,
    mutant_analysis,
    residue_mut_id
  ) %>%
  head(20)

# ============================================================
# Predictor definitions
# ============================================================

EVcouplings_predictor_info <- tibble(
  
  predictor = c(
    "EVcouplings_frequency",
    "EVcouplings_conservation",
    "EVcouplings_independent",
    "EVcouplings_epistatic"
  ),
  
  predictor_name = c(
    "Frequency",
    "Conservation",
    "Independent model",
    "Epistatic model"
  ),
  
  # Direction expected relative to replication score
  #
  # +1: higher predictor score -> higher replication
  # -1: higher predictor score -> lower replication
  direction = c(
     1,
    -1,
     1,
     1
  )
)

EVcouplings_predictor_info
# # A tibble: 4 × 3
#   predictor                predictor_name    direction
#   <chr>                    <chr>                 <dbl>
# 1 EVcouplings_frequency    Frequency                 1
# 2 EVcouplings_conservation Conservation             -1
# 3 EVcouplings_independent  Independent model         1
# 4 EVcouplings_epistatic    Epistatic model           1


# ============================================================
# 3. Calculate proteome-wide Spearman correlations
# ============================================================

EVcouplings_DMS_spearman <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    EVcouplings_predictor_info$predictor,
    function(pred) {

      df <-
        phix_proteome_dms_mut_modelling_merged_EVcouplings %>%

        filter(
          is.finite(
            .data[[pred]]
          ),
          is.finite(
            fitness_aa_mut
          )
        )

      test <-
        cor.test(
          df[[pred]],
          df$fitness_aa_mut,
          method = "spearman",
          exact = FALSE
        )

      tibble(
        predictor = pred,

        n =
          nrow(df),

        spearman_rho =
          unname(
            test$estimate
          ),

        p_value =
          test$p.value
      )
    }
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    EVcouplings_predictor_info,
    by = "predictor"
  ) %>%

  select(
    predictor,
    predictor_name,
    n,
    spearman_rho,
    p_value
  )

EVcouplings_DMS_spearman
# # A tibble: 4 × 5
#   predictor                predictor_name        n spearman_rho   p_value
#   <chr>                    <chr>             <int>        <dbl>     <dbl>
# 1 EVcouplings_frequency    Frequency         21873        0.179 1.67e-156
# 2 EVcouplings_conservation Conservation      21873       -0.244 1.57e-293
# 3 EVcouplings_independent  Independent model 21873        0.178 7.99e-156
# 4 EVcouplings_epistatic    Epistatic model   21873        0.319 0        


# Add FDR-adjusted P-values
EVcouplings_DMS_spearman <-
  EVcouplings_DMS_spearman %>%

  mutate(
    p_adjust_FDR =
      p.adjust(
        p_value,
        method = "BH"
      )
  )

EVcouplings_DMS_spearman

#   predictor                predictor_name        n spearman_rho   p_value p_adjust_FDR

# 1 EVcouplings_frequency    Frequency         21873        0.179 1.67e-156    2.23e-156
# 2 EVcouplings_conservation Conservation      21873       -0.244 1.57e-293    3.14e-293
# 3 EVcouplings_independent  Independent model 21873        0.178 7.99e-156    7.99e-156
# 4 EVcouplings_epistatic    Epistatic model   21873        0.319 0            0        


# ============================================================
# 4. Calculate correlations separately for every protein
# ============================================================

EVcouplings_DMS_long <-
  phix_proteome_dms_mut_modelling_merged_EVcouplings %>%

  select(
    residue_mut_id,
    aa_mut_gene,
    fitness_aa_mut,
    all_of(
      EVcouplings_predictor_info$predictor
    )
  ) %>%

  pivot_longer(
    cols =
      all_of(
        EVcouplings_predictor_info$predictor
      ),

    names_to =
      "predictor",

    values_to =
      "predictor_score"
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    EVcouplings_predictor_info,
    by = "predictor"
  )


EVcouplings_DMS_spearman_by_protein <-
  EVcouplings_DMS_long %>%
  
  group_by(
    aa_mut_gene,
    predictor,
    predictor_name,
    direction
  ) %>%
  
  summarise(
    
    n = sum(
      is.finite(predictor_score) &
      is.finite(fitness_aa_mut)
    ),
    
    rho_raw = {
      
      valid <-
        is.finite(predictor_score) &
        is.finite(fitness_aa_mut)
      
      if (
        sum(valid) >= 3 &&
        length(unique(predictor_score[valid])) > 1 &&
        length(unique(fitness_aa_mut[valid])) > 1
      ) {
        
        cor(
          predictor_score[valid],
          fitness_aa_mut[valid],
          method = "spearman"
        )
        
      } else {
        
        NA_real_
      }
    },
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(
    
    # Direction-normalized correlation
    performance_rho =
      rho_raw * direction
  )

      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3,
    angle = 90,
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(
      min(
        EVcouplings_dot_plot_df$performance_rho,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      
      max(
        EVcouplings_dot_plot_df$performance_rho,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) + 0.12
    ),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  
  theme_classic() +
  
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    
    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 15,
      r = 10,
      b = 10,
      l = 10
    )
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    #y = "Direction-adjusted Spearman rho",
    y = "Direction-adjusted Spearman rho",
    
    color = "Protein",
    title = expression(Phi*X174~alignment-derived~predictor~performance~(EVcouplings)),
    subtitle = "Each dot is one protein \nred crossbar = median across proteins \nred dashed line = RSA (monomer)"
  )
```

### 1) ESCOTT
- Tekpinar M, David L, Henry T, Carbone A. PRESCOTT: a population aware, epistatic, and structural model accurately predicts missense effects. Genome Biol. 2025 May 6;26(1):113. doi: 10.1186/s13059-025-03581-y. PMID: 40329382; PMCID: PMC12054230.
```{r}
# Function to load ESCOTT data
load_escott_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path) {

  # ---- read file ----
  df <- read.delim(
    file_path,
    header = FALSE,
    sep = "",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ---- shift WT annotation row right ----
  df[1, ] <- c(NA, as.character(df[1, -ncol(df)]))

  # ---- split WT row and score rows ----
  wt_row   <- df[1, ]
  score_df <- df[-1, ]

  # substitutions (a, c, d, ...)
  subs <- score_df[[1]]
  score_df <- score_df[, -1]

  # force numeric scores
  score_df[] <- lapply(score_df, as.numeric)

  # ---- extract WT info (aligned to score columns) ----
  wt_vec <- as.character(wt_row[-1])
  wt_vec <- wt_vec[!is.na(wt_vec)]

  wt_aa  <- sub("[0-9]+", "", wt_vec)
  wt_pos <- seq_along(wt_aa)

  # ---- long-format transform ----
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)

  out <- score_df %>%
    mutate(sub = subs) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -sub,
      names_to = "col",
      values_to = "score"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      col_idx = match(col, colnames(score_df)),
      pos     = wt_pos[col_idx],
      mutant  = paste0(wt_aa[col_idx], pos, toupper(sub)),
      aa_mut_id = mutant,
      ESCOTT = score
    ) %>%
    select(mutant, aa_mut_id, pos, score, ESCOTT)

  return(out)
}
```

### 2) PoET, MSA
- The sequences, owing to their shared evolutionary ties, inherently embed information about the protein’s local fitness landscape. PoET utilizes this information to assess the probability of observing a specific sequence based on the inferred evolutionary process.
- Timothy F. Jr Truong and Tristan Bepler. Poet: a generative model of protein families as sequences-of-sequences. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (Vol. 36), 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2306.06156, arXiv:2306.06156.

```{r}
# Function to load the data
load_poet_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path, gene, score_col = "score") {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id = mutant,
      PoET = .data[[score_col]]
    )

  return(df)
}
```

### 3) RSALOR, Structure + MSA
- The rsalor package combines structural data (Relative Solvent Accessibility, RSA) and evolutionary data (Log Odd Ratio, LOR from MSA) to evaluate effects of missense mutations in proteins. It computes the RSA*LOR score for each single-site missense mutation in a target protein by combining multiple computational steps into a fast and user-friendly tool. 
- Matsvei Tsishyn, Pauline Hermans, Marianne Rooman, Fabrizio Pucci (2025). Residue conservation and solvent accessibility are (almost) all you need for predicting mutational effects in proteins. Bioinformatics, 41(6), btaf322. https://github.com/3BioCompBio/RSALOR 

```{r}
# Function to load RSALOR benchmarking results
load_rsalor_benchmarking_data <- function(
  file_path, 
  gene, 
  structure_source = NULL, 
  score_col = "RSA.LOR",
  flip_sign = TRUE
) {
  
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id = mutation_fasta,
      structure_source = structure_source,
      RSALOR = as.numeric(.data[[score_col]])
    )

  if (flip_sign) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(RSALOR = -RSALOR)
  }

  return(df)
}
```

### 4-5) GEMME MSA + ProteoCast
- ProteoCast relies on GEMME, a highly efficient, unsupervised, and fully interpretable variant effect predictor (Laine et al., 2019). By focusing on how protein residues segregate along the topology of evolutionary trees, GEMME has proven instrumental for studying protein stability, function, and disease mechanisms in several studies -- see, for instance, Tsuboyama et al., 2023. It was extensively tested against over 2.5M experimental measurements (Abakarova et al., 2023, Laine et al., 2019). It is among the top-performing methods on the widely adopted ProteinGym benchmark. 
- Official GEMMA Link https://www.lcqb.upmc.fr/GEMME/submit.html 
- ProteoCast https://proteocast.ijm.fr/results/search/, give interactive heatmaps + Mutational Landscape + Input Alignment + Raw Score Distribution + Sensitivity profile + 3D Structure
- Load results from ProteoCast, provided both GEMME scores and scores weighted by RSA.

```{r}
# Function to load ProteoCast data
load_proteocast_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path, gene, score_col = "Variant_score", rsa_score_col = "RSA.Variant_score") {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  #df <- read.csv2(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id = Mutation,
      GEMME = .data[[score_col]],
      ProteoCast = .data[[rsa_score_col]]
    )

  return(df)
}
```

### 6) ProSST-2048 (VenusFactory2)
- It employs a structure quantization module to convert 3D protein structures into discrete tokens using a GVP encoder and k-means clustering, coupled with a Transformer architecture featuring sequence-structure disentangled attention. The model explicitly learns residue-structure relationships, enabling robust predictions even for stability, binding, and expression-related mutations.
- Run ProSST-2048 in VenusFactory2

```{r}
# Function
load_VenusFactory_data <- function(
  file_path,
  predictor = "ProSST_2048",
  structure_source = NULL,
  gene = NULL
) {

  df <- read.csv(
    file_path,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  m <- stringr::str_match(
    df$Mutant,
    "^([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])$"
  )

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_wt  = m[, 2],
      aa_mut_pos = as.integer(m[, 3]),
      aa_mut_sub = m[, 4],
      aa_mut_id  = paste0(aa_mut_wt, aa_mut_pos, aa_mut_sub),
      structure_source = structure_source
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      !!predictor := `Prediction Score`
    )

  return(df)

}
```

### 9-10) VESPA
- VESPA is a simple, yet powerful Single Amino Acid Variant (SAV) effect predictor based on embeddings of the Protein Language Model ProtT5. The specifics of VESPA and VESPAl can be found in our paper, Embeddings from protein language models predict conservation and variant effects (Marquet et al., 2021). The performance of VESPA when evaluated against SOTA methods can be seen below.
- https://github.com/Rostlab/VESPA

```{r}
# Function to load VESPA benchmarking scores
load_vespa_full_benchmarking_data <- function(
  file_path,
  gene,
  full_score_col = "VESPA",
  light_score_col = "VESPAl",
  flip_sign = TRUE
) {

  df <- read.csv2(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # ---- Fix Mutant indexing: M0A -> M1A ----
  parsed <- stringr::str_match(df$Mutant, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Mutant = ifelse(
        !is.na(parsed[,1]),
        paste0(
          parsed[,2],
          as.integer(parsed[,3]) + 1,
          parsed[,4]
        ),
        Mutant
      ),

      # ---- standardized mutation ID ----
      aa_mut_id = Mutant,

      # ---- metadata + scores ----
      gene = gene,
      VESPA = as.numeric(.data[[full_score_col]]),
      VESPAl = as.numeric(.data[[light_score_col]])
    )

  # ---- Optional sign flip ----
  if (flip_sign) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        VESPA = -VESPA,
        VESPAl = -VESPAl
      )
  }

  return(df)
}
```

### 13) EVmutation2
- Thomas A. Hopf, Artem Gazizov, Sergio Garcia Busto, Ethan Eschbach, SunJae Lee, Milot Mirdita, Rose Orenbuch, Khaoula Belahsen, David Ross, Chris Sander, Martin Steinegger, Simon d’Oelsnitz, Debora S. Marks. evedesign: accessible biosequence design with a unified framework. bioRxiv 2026.03.17.712115; doi: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.17.712115
- https://github.com/debbiemarkslab/EVmutation, This package has been superseded by the EVcouplings package, which covers the full computational pipeline including alignment generation, 3D structure prediction, and more.
- https://evedesign.bio/

```{r}
# Function to load the ESM2 and EVmutation2 prediction results
load_esm2_evMut2_data <- function(file_path, predictor = NULL, gene = NULL) {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(df) <- c("predictor_id", predictor, "predictor_mut_seq")
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      gene = gene,
      # Split predictor_id by "_"
      id_parts = str_split(predictor_id, "_"),
      aa_mut_pos = as.numeric(sapply(id_parts, `[`, 2)),
      aa_mut_wt      = sapply(id_parts, `[`, 3),
      aa_mut_sub     = sapply(id_parts, `[`, 4),
      aa_mut_id  = paste0(aa_mut_wt, aa_mut_pos, aa_mut_sub)
    ) %>%
    select(-id_parts)  # clean up temporary column
  
  return(df)
}
```

### 14) SaProt (650M)
- a “structure-aware vocabulary” that integrates residue tokens with structure tokens. The structure tokens are derived by encoding the 3D structure of proteins using Foldseek. SaProt, a large-scale general-purpose PLM trained on an extensive dataset comprising approximately 40 million protein sequences and structures. 
- Su, J., Li, Z., Tao, T. et al. Democratizing protein language model training, sharing and collaboration. Nat Biotechnol (2025). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-025-02859-7
- https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProt
- the aa positions need to shift, because the original results always start from 1

```{r}
# Function to load SaProt benchmarking scores
load_saprot_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path, gene, structure_source, score_col = "score") {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  #df <- read.csv2(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id= mutation,
      structure_source = structure_source,
      SaProt_650M_AF2 = .data[[score_col]]
    )

  return(df)
}
```

### 15-20) ESM2 (8M, 35M, 150M, 650M, 3B, 15B)
- SOTA general-purpose protein language model. Can be used to predict structure, function and other protein properties directly from individual sequences. Released with Lin et al. 2022 (Aug 2022 update). our state-of-the-art ESM-2 and ESMFold, as well as MSA Transformer, ESM-1v for predicting variant effects and ESM-IF1 for inverse folding ... 
- 'ESM-2 outperforms all tested single-sequence protein language models across a range of structure prediction tasks. ESMFold harnesses the ESM-2 language model to generate accurate structure predictions end to end directly from the sequence of a protein.'
- https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm?tab=readme-ov-file


### 22) DDMut-PPI
DDMut-PPI: Protein affinity;
- Yunzhuo Zhou, YooChan Myung, Carlos H M Rodrigues, David B Ascher, DDMut-PPI: predicting effects of mutations on protein–protein interactions using graph-based deep learning, Nucleic Acids Research, Volume 52, Issue W1, 5 July 2024, Pages W207–W214, https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae412

#### 22.1) Interface Analysis
```{r}
# Function to prepare DDMut-PPI Affinity predictions
prepare_ddmut_ppi_results <- function(ddmut_df, aa_name_map) {
  ddmut_df <- ddmut_df %>%
    mutate(
      aa_from = aa_name_map[toupper(wild.type)],
      aa_to   = aa_name_map[toupper(mutant)],
      aa_mut_id = paste0(aa_from, res.number, aa_to),
      ddmut_mut_id = paste(chain, aa_mut_id, sep = " ")
    ) %>%
    rename(
      DDMut_PPI = ddmut.ppi.forward.prediction,
      DDMut_PPI_rev = ddmut.ppi.reverse.prediction
    )
  
  return(ddmut_df)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to load and process DDMut-PPI ddG affinity prediction files
load_ddmut_ppi_data <- function(protein_code, base_path = "./codes_Github_final/data/predictors_data/000_DDMut_PPI_ddG_affinity", aa_name_map) {
  # Construct full path
  path <- file.path(base_path, protein_code)
  
  # List CSV files
  csv_files <- list.files(path = path, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(csv_files) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No files found for", protein_code, "in", path))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Read and combine CSVs
  data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(csv_files, read.csv))
  
  # Process using the provided amino acid mapping
  data <- prepare_ddmut_ppi_results(data, aa_name_map)
  
  # Print duplicate information
  dup_table <- table(duplicated(data$ddmut_mut_id))
  print(paste(protein_code, "- Duplicated ddmut_mut_id:"))
  print(dup_table)
  
  return(data)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to load and process DDMut ddG stability prediction files
load_ddmut_example_data <- function(folder_path) {
  csv_files <- list.files(
    path = folder_path,
    pattern = "\\.csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )

  df <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(csv_files, read.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ddmut_mut_id = paste0(chain, " ", aa_from, position, aa_to)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      DDMut = prediction,
      DDMut_rev = prediction_reverse
    )

  return(df)
}


load_ddmut_data <- function(protein_code, pdb_code, base_path = "./codes_Github_final/data/predictors_data/000_DDMut_ddG_stability/") {
  # Construct path to folder
  folder_name <- paste0(protein_code, "_", pdb_code)
  path <- file.path(base_path, folder_name)
  
  # List and read all CSV files
  csv_files <- list.files(path = path, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(csv_files) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No files found in", path))
    return(NULL)
  }

  data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(csv_files, read.csv))
  
  # Create mutation identifier
  data$ddmut_mut_id <- paste0(data$chain, " ", data$aa_from, data$position, data$aa_to)
  
  # Optionally rename the prediction column
  if ("prediction" %in% colnames(data)) {
    data <- data %>% rename(DDMut = prediction,
                            DDMut_rev = prediction_reverse)
  }
  
  # Report duplicates
  dup_table <- table(duplicated(data$ddmut_mut_id))
  print(paste(folder_name, "- Duplicated IDs:"))
  print(dup_table)
  
  return(data)
}
```

- https://neurosnap.ai/service/ProteinMPNN-ddG

```{r}
# Function to prepare ProteinMPNN_ddG data
prepare_proteinmpnn_ddG_results <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      mut_id = paste(Pre, Position, Post, sep = ""),
      ddmut_mut_id = paste(Chain, mut_id, sep = " ")
    ) %>%
    rename(
      ProteinMPNN_ddG = ProteinMPNN.ddG.Score
    )
  return(df)
}
```

### 26) ThermoMPNN
- H. Dieckhaus,M. Brocidiacono,N.Z. Randolph, & B. Kuhlman,  Transfer learning to leverage larger datasets for improved prediction of protein stability changes, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 121 (6) e2314853121, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2314853121 (2024).

```{r}
# Function to load the ThermoMPNN prediction data and correct the aa positions
load_thermompnn_data <- function(
  file_path, 
  position_offset = 0,
  flip_sign = TRUE
) {

  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # ---- Standardize column names ----
  names(df) <- c("row", "aa_mut_ID", "ThermoMPNN", "position", "aa_from", "aa_to")

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # ---- Fix position ----
      position = as.integer(position) + position_offset,

      # ---- Standard mutation ID ----
      aa_mut_id = paste0(aa_from, position, aa_to),

      # ---- Ensure numeric ----
      ThermoMPNN = as.numeric(ThermoMPNN)
    )

  # ---- Optional sign flip ----
  if (flip_sign) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(ThermoMPNN = -ThermoMPNN)
  }

  return(df)
}
```

```{r}
  mutate(
```
```{r}
    mutant = str_replace(
      mutant,
      "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])",
      function(x) {
        wt  <- str_extract(x, "^[A-Z]")
        pos <- as.numeric(str_extract(x, "\\d+"))
        mut <- str_extract(x, "[A-Z]$")
        paste0(wt, pos - 1, mut)
      }
    ),
    protein = "F"
  ) %>%
  filter(as.numeric(str_extract(mutant, "\\d+")) > 0)
```

### 00) RSASA, structural baselines
RSASA as baseline, to predicting the mutational effects by surface accessibility;

- RSASA vs Mutations (only single ORF 1aa mutations)
```{r}
# Function to prepare RSASA predictions
prepare_mut_RSASA_baselines <- function(data) {
  
  safe_pmax <- function(df, pattern) {
    cols <- select(df, ends_with(pattern))
    if (ncol(cols) == 0) {
      return(NA_real_)  # no matching columns
    } else {
      return(do.call(pmax, c(cols, na.rm = TRUE)))
    }
  }
  
  data %>%
    filter(aa_mut_class == "Missense") %>%
    mutate(
      #RSASA_monomer_rescaled = safe_pmax(., "_aa_monomer_RSASA2"),
      RSASA_complex          = safe_pmax(., "_binderS_aa_RSASA"),
      #dRSASA_complex         = safe_pmax(., "_binderS_aa_dRSASA"),
      RSASA_monomer          = safe_pmax(., "_aa_monomer_RSASA")
    ) %>%
    select(
      aa_mut_pos,
      aa_mut_gene,
      aa_mut_structure,
      aa_mut_wt,
      aa_mut_sub,
      phix_aa_mut_orf_class,
      fitness_aa_mut,
      
      #RSASA_monomer_rescaled,
      RSASA_monomer,
      RSASA_complex
      #dRSASA_complex,
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Function to process RSASA data
process_RSASA_data <- function(gp_data) {
  # Step 1: Set column names
  names(gp_data) <- c("aa_wt_info", "RSASA", "col_to_remove")
  
  # Step 2: Extract mutation position and mutation wild-type information
  gp_data <- gp_data %>%
    mutate(
      aa_mut_pos = as.numeric(str_split_fixed(aa_wt_info, "`", 2)[, 2]),
      aa_mut_wt = as.character(str_split_fixed(aa_wt_info, "/", 6)[, 5]),
      RSASA = as.numeric(str_sub(RSASA, 1, -2))
    )
  
  # Step 3: Select relevant columns
  gp_data_to_bind <- gp_data %>%
    select(aa_mut_pos, RSASA)
  
  return(gp_data_to_bind)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to skip models not applied and to prevent NA and characters in score columns
prepare_structure_predictions_long <- function(df,
                             model_cols,
                             gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
                             fit_col = "fitness_aa_mut",
                             rescaled_col = "fitness_modelling_rescaled",
                             name_col = "model_name",
                             value_col = "prediction_score") {

  # keep only model columns that exist
  model_cols_present <- intersect(model_cols, colnames(df))

  df %>%
    # Step 1: keep fitness as-is (no rescaling)
    dplyr::mutate(
      !!rescaled_col := .data[[fit_col]]
    ) %>%
    # Step 2: coerce model columns to numeric
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(model_cols_present),
        ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))
      )
    ) %>%
    # Step 3: Pivot to long format
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::all_of(model_cols_present),
      names_to = name_col,
      values_to = value_col
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Function to process mutant id
add_mutation_columns <- function(df, mutant_col = "mutant") {

  m <- stringr::str_match(df[[mutant_col]], "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")

  df$aa_mut_wt  <- m[, 2]
  df$aa_mut_pos <- as.integer(m[, 3])
  df$aa_mut_sub <- m[, 4]
  df$aa_mut_id  <- paste0(df$aa_mut_wt, df$aa_mut_pos, df$aa_mut_sub)

  df
}

technical_control_blat_sign_check_results <- technical_control_blat_sign_check_map %>%
  mutate(
    spearman_r = purrr::map2_dbl(my_col, pg_col, function(col1, col2) {

      x <- technical_control_blat_proteinGym_merged[[col1]]
      y <- technical_control_blat_proteinGym_merged[[col2]]

      keep <- !(is.na(x) | is.na(y))

      if (sum(keep) < 10) return(NA_real_)

      suppressWarnings(cor(x[keep], y[keep], method = "spearman"))
    })
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sign_status = case_when(
      is.na(spearman_r) ~ "NA",
      spearman_r > 0.2 ~ "correct",
      spearman_r < -0.2 ~ "reversed",
      TRUE ~ "unclear"
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# Function to load proteinGym datasets 
load_proteingym_dataset <- function(file_path, predictors = predictors_tested) {
  
  library(data.table)
  
  cols_needed <- c("mutant", "DMS_score", predictors)
  
  df <- fread(file_path, select = cols_needed, showProgress = FALSE)
  
  df <- as.data.frame(df)
  
  df_long <- df %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(predictors),
      names_to = "predictor_col",
      values_to = "prediction"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dataset = basename(file_path)
    )
  
  return(df_long)
}

# define predictors
predictors_tested <- c("ESCOTT", "PoET", "RSALOR", "GEMME", "ProSST-2048", "ESM-IF1", "MIFST", "VESPA", "VESPAl", "Tranception_L_no_retrieval", "Tranception_L", "SaProt_650M_AF2", "ESM2_8M", "ESM2_35M", "ESM2_150M", "ESM2_650M", "ESM2_3B", "ESM2_15B", "ESM1v_single", "ESM1v_ensemble", "ESM3", "ESMC-300M", "ESMC-600M", "Progen2_large", "Progen2_xlarge")

# load viral predictions
folder_path_proteingym_zero_shot_virus <- "./codes_Github_final/data/predictors_data/999_ProteinGym_benchmarking/ProteinGym_zero_shot_substitutions_scores_virus"
files_proteingym_zero_shot_virus <- list.files(folder_path_proteingym_zero_shot_virus, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

proteingym_zero_shot_virus <- purrr::map_dfr(files_proteingym_zero_shot_virus, load_proteingym_dataset, predictors = predictors_tested)
```

```{r}
    predictor_target,
    
    # keep as-is (no fake averaging)
    mean_rho   = value,
    median_rho = value,
    sd_spearman_rho = NA_real_,
    n_datasets = 1,
    
    predictor_input_modality,
    predictor_rank_by_virus,
    predictor_rank_average,
    
    predictor_input_modality_simplified = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("RSA", predictor_input_modality, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "RSA",
      TRUE ~ predictor_input_modality_simplified
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(mean_rho))
```

## ESM-IF1, single chains VS. multi-chains
```{r}
# load ESM-IF1 complex data
esm_if1_dir <-
  "./codes_Github_final/data/predictors_data/006_VenusREM_scores_260526/ESM-IF1_complex"


# ============================================================
# ESM-IF1 complex-aware results
# ============================================================

esm_if1_complex_files <-
  list.files(
    esm_if1_dir,
    pattern = "_single_vs_complex\\.csv$",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )

esm_if1_complex_files

length(esm_if1_complex_files)
# [1] 17


# ============================================================
# Load all single-vs-complex results
# ============================================================

esm_if1_complex_results <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    esm_if1_complex_files,
    function(file) {

      df <-
        data.table::fread(
          file
        ) %>%
        as.data.frame()


      filename <-
        basename(
          file
        )


      folder <-
        dirname(
          file
        )


      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Structure
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      structure <-
        dplyr::case_when(

          grepl(
            "1cd3",
            folder,
            ignore.case = TRUE
          ) ~
            "1CD3",

          grepl(
            "2bpa",
            folder,
            ignore.case = TRUE
          ) ~
            "2BPA",

          grepl(
            "4jpp",
            folder,
            ignore.case = TRUE
          ) ~
            "4JPP",

          grepl(
            "8g02",
            folder,
            ignore.case = TRUE
          ) ~
            "8G02",

          TRUE ~
            NA_character_
        )


      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Remove filename suffix
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      sample_name <-
        sub(
          "_single_vs_complex\\.csv$",
          "",
          filename
        )


      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Target chain
      #
      # Examples:
      # C001_D1 -> C001
      # A_H1    -> A
      # C_E1    -> C
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      target_chain <-
        sub(
          "_.*$",
          "",
          sample_name
        )


      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Structure copy
      #
      # Examples:
      # C001_D1 -> D1
      # C005_B  -> B
      # A_H1    -> H1
      # C_E1    -> E1
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      structure_copy <-
        sub(
          "^[^_]+_",
          "",
          sample_name
        )


      # --------------------------------------------------------
      # Protein
      #
      # D1 -> D
      # H2 -> H
      # E1 -> E
      # F  -> F
      # --------------------------------------------------------

      protein <-
        sub(
          "[0-9]+$",
          "",
          structure_copy
        )


      df %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          structure = structure,
          protein = protein,
          target_chain = target_chain,
          structure_copy = structure_copy,
          source_file = filename,
          source_path = file
        )
    }
  )

dim(
  esm_if1_complex_results
)
# [1] 52520    21

names(
  esm_if1_complex_results
)

head(
  esm_if1_complex_results
)

esm_if1_complex_results %>%
  dplyr::count(
    structure,
    protein,
    target_chain,
    structure_copy
  )

# Keep only the structural copies we want
esm_if1_complex_selected <-
  esm_if1_complex_results %>%

  dplyr::filter(
    !is_wt_substitution
  ) %>%

  # For 4JPP protein H, use only chain C / H3
  dplyr::filter(
    structure != "4JPP" |
      target_chain == "C"
  )

esm_if1_complex_selected %>%
  dplyr::count(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    target_chain
  )



# ============================================================
# Earlier 1CD3 single-chain saturation results
# ============================================================

esm_if1_singlechain_files <-
  list.files(
    file.path(
      esm_if1_dir,
      "results_of_single_chain_1cd3_inputs"
    ),
    pattern = "_saturation_results\\.csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )

esm_if1_singlechain_files

esm_if1_singlechain_1cd3 <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    esm_if1_singlechain_files,
    function(file) {

      df <-
        data.table::fread(
          file
        ) %>%
        as.data.frame()


      filename <-
        basename(
          file
        )


      chain <-
        sub(
          "_1CD3.*$",
          "",
          filename
        )


      protein <-
        dplyr::case_when(

          chain %in%
            c(
              "1",
              "2",
              "3",
              "4"
            ) ~
            "D",

          chain == "B" ~
            "B",

          chain == "F" ~
            "F",

          chain == "G" ~
            "G",

          TRUE ~
            NA_character_
        )


      structure_copy <-
        dplyr::case_when(

          chain == "1" ~ "D1",
          chain == "2" ~ "D2",
          chain == "3" ~ "D3",
          chain == "4" ~ "D4",
          chain == "B" ~ "B",
          chain == "F" ~ "F",
          chain == "G" ~ "G",

          TRUE ~
            NA_character_
        )


      df %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          structure = "1CD3",
          protein = protein,
          original_chain = chain,
          structure_copy = structure_copy,
          source_file = filename,
          source_path = file
        )
    }
  )

# A tibble: 0 × 5
# ℹ 5 variables: protein <chr>, aa_mut_wt <chr>, aa_mut_pos <int>, aa_mut_sub <chr>, n <int>


# ============================================================
# 2. Prepare complex-aware ESM-IF1 results
# ============================================================

# First inspect the structure → biological position offsets
esm_if1_position_offsets <-
  esm_if1_complex_selected %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    target_chain,
    aa_mut_pos,
    pdb_res_id
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    position_offset =
      as.integer(pdb_res_id) -
      as.integer(aa_mut_pos)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    target_chain
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_positions =
      dplyr::n(),

    min_offset =
      min(
        position_offset,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    max_offset =
      max(
        position_offset,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    offsets =
      paste(
        sort(
          unique(
            position_offset
          )
        ),
        collapse = ","
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

esm_if1_position_offsets

#  8 2BPA      F       F              C001                 426          0          0 0      
#  9 2BPA      G       G              C002                 175          0          0 0      
# 10 2BPA      J       J              C003                  36          1          1 1      
# 11 4JPP      H       H3             C                    122          4          4 4      
# 12 8G02      E       E1             C                     65          1          1 1      
# 13 8G02      E       E2             D                     65          1          1 1      


# ============================================================
# 3. Correct ESM-IF1 positions
# ============================================================

esm_if1_complex_corrected <-
  esm_if1_complex_results %>%

  # remove WT substitutions
  dplyr::filter(
    !is_wt_substitution
  ) %>%

  # For protein H, only retain chain C / H3
  dplyr::filter(
    structure != "4JPP" |
      target_chain == "C"
  ) %>%

  # preserve original ESM-sequence position
  dplyr::rename(
    aa_mut_pos_structure = aa_mut_pos,
    aa_mut_id_structure = aa_mut_id
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(

    aa_mut_pos_structure =
      as.integer(aa_mut_pos_structure),

    pdb_res_id =
      as.integer(pdb_res_id),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Convert structural/ESM numbering to ΦX174 protein numbering
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    aa_mut_pos =
      dplyr::case_when(

        # 1CD3 protein D
        structure == "1CD3" &
          protein == "D" &
          structure_copy == "D1" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 5L,

        structure == "1CD3" &
          protein == "D" &
          structure_copy == "D2" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 5L,

        structure == "1CD3" &
          protein == "D" &
          structure_copy == "D3" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 4L,

        structure == "1CD3" &
          protein == "D" &
          structure_copy == "D4" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 6L,

        # 1CD3 protein B
        structure == "1CD3" &
          protein == "B" &
          aa_mut_pos_structure >= 9L ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 52L,

        structure == "1CD3" &
          protein == "B" &
          aa_mut_pos_structure < 9L ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure,

        # 2BPA protein J
        structure == "2BPA" &
          protein == "J" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 1L,

        # 4JPP protein H, chain C only
        structure == "4JPP" &
          protein == "H" &
          target_chain == "C" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 146L,

        # 8G02 protein E
        structure == "8G02" &
          protein == "E" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure + 1L,

        # F, G and unaffected proteins
        TRUE ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure
      ),

    # corrected mutation identity
    aa_mut_id =
      paste0(
        aa_mut_wt,
        aa_mut_pos,
        aa_mut_sub
      ),

    gene_aa_mut_ID =
      paste0(
        "gp",
        protein,
        "_",
        aa_mut_wt,
        aa_mut_pos,
        aa_mut_sub
      ),

    structure_instance =
      paste(
        structure,
        structure_copy,
        sep = "_"
      )
  )

# QC the corrected numbering against your DMS sequence
dms_residue_reference <-
  phix_proteins_dms_mut_modelling_merged_collapsed %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    protein =
      as.character(aa_mut_gene),

    aa_mut_pos =
      as.integer(aa_mut_pos),

    dms_aa_wt =
      as.character(aa_mut_wt)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()


# Join by the corrected position
esm_if1_position_qc <-
  esm_if1_complex_corrected %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    target_chain,
    aa_mut_pos_structure,
    pdb_res_id,
    aa_mut_pos,
    aa_mut_wt
  ) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(
    dms_residue_reference,
    by = c(
      "protein",
      "aa_mut_pos"
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    wt_matches =
      aa_mut_wt ==
      dms_aa_wt
  )

esm_if1_position_qc %>%
  dplyr::count(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    wt_matches
  )

# For E, explicitly verify that the corrected position agrees with pdb_res_id
esm_if1_position_qc %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    structure == "8G02",
    protein == "E"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(
    structure_copy,
    corrected_matches_pdb
  )
#   structure_copy corrected_matches_pdb  n
# 1             E1                  TRUE 65
# 2             E2                  TRUE 65


# ============================================================
# Patch our current corrected dataset
# For 8G02 E, the first ESM-IF1 residue appears to be an extra N-terminal 'G' residue that is not part of the ΦX174 E sequence we are analysing.
# 1) remove aa_mut_pos_structure == 1 for E;
# 2) do not shift the remaining positions;
# 3) therefore structure position 2 (V) becomes biological position 2, structure position 3 (R) becomes biological position 3, etc.;
# 4) rebuild aa_mut_id and gene_aa_mut_ID.
# ============================================================

esm_if1_complex_corrected <-
  esm_if1_complex_corrected %>%

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Protein E / 8G02:
  # remove extra N-terminal residue present in structure input
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  dplyr::filter(
    !(
      structure == "8G02" &
        protein == "E" &
        aa_mut_pos_structure == 1L
    )
  ) %>%

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Correct biological position for E
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  dplyr::mutate(

    aa_mut_pos =
      dplyr::case_when(

        structure == "8G02" &
          protein == "E" ~
          aa_mut_pos_structure,

        TRUE ~
          aa_mut_pos
      ),

    # rebuild mutation IDs
    aa_mut_id =
      paste0(
        aa_mut_wt,
        aa_mut_pos,
        aa_mut_sub
      ),

    gene_aa_mut_ID =
      paste0(
        "gp",
        protein,
        "_",
        aa_mut_wt,
        aa_mut_pos,
        aa_mut_sub
      )
  )

# Re-run the WT-sequence QC
esm_if1_position_qc <-
  esm_if1_complex_corrected %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    target_chain,
    aa_mut_pos_structure,
    pdb_res_id,
    aa_mut_pos,
    aa_mut_wt
  ) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(
    dms_residue_reference,
    by = c(
      "protein",
      "aa_mut_pos"
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    wt_matches =
      aa_mut_wt ==
      dms_aa_wt
  )

esm_if1_complex_dms <-

# check the matching again

# 1) Correlation with experimental replication scores
esm_if1_dms_correlations <-
  esm_if1_complex_dms_complete %>%

  dplyr::group_by(
    structure,
    protein,
    structure_copy,
    structure_instance
  ) %>%

  dplyr::summarise(
    n =
      dplyr::n(),

    rho_single =
      stats::cor(
        delta_ll_single,
        fitness_aa_mut,
        method = "spearman"
      ),

    rho_complex =
      stats::cor(
        delta_ll_complex,
        fitness_aa_mut,
        method = "spearman"
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(
    delta_rho =
      rho_complex -
      rho_single
  )

      stats::median(
        rho_single,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_rho_complex =
      stats::median(
        rho_complex,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_delta_rho =
      stats::median(
        delta_rho,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    n_complex_better =
      sum(
        delta_rho > 0,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    n_single_better =
      sum(
        delta_rho < 0,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    pct_complex_better =
      100 *
      mean(
        delta_rho > 0,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  )
```

```{r}
missing_evo2 <- phix_evo2_fitness %>%
  filter(
    is.na(evo2_7b_base) |
    is.na(evo2_7b_microviridae)
  )

print(nrow(missing_evo2))
# [1] 0


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Correlation analysis: all variants and by Hamming distance
# ------------------------------------------------------------

correlation_data <- phix_evo2_fitness %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(fitness_final),
    is.finite(evo2_7b_base),
    is.finite(evo2_7b_microviridae)
  )

calculate_correlations <- function(df) {

  tibble(
    n = nrow(df),

    base_pearson = cor(
      df$fitness_final,
      df$evo2_7b_base,
      method = "pearson"
    ),

    base_spearman = cor(
      df$fitness_final,
      df$evo2_7b_base,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    micro_pearson = cor(
      df$fitness_final,
      df$evo2_7b_microviridae,
      method = "pearson"
    ),

    micro_spearman = cor(
      df$fitness_final,
      df$evo2_7b_microviridae,
      method = "spearman"
    )
  )
}

# All variants
correlation_all <- calculate_correlations(correlation_data) %>%
  mutate(group = "All variants", .before = 1)

# Separately for 1-, 2-, and 3-nt variants
correlation_by_hamming <- correlation_data %>%
  group_by(genome_nt_mut_ham) %>%
  group_modify(~ calculate_correlations(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    group = paste0(genome_nt_mut_ham, "-nt"),
    .before = 1
  ) %>%
  select(-genome_nt_mut_ham)

# Combine
correlation_summary <- bind_rows(
  correlation_all,
  correlation_by_hamming
)

correlation_summary
# # A tibble: 4 × 6
#   group            n base_pearson base_spearman micro_pearson micro_spearman
#   <chr>        <int>        <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl>          <dbl>
# 1 All variants 44195        0.432         0.495         0.371          0.461
# 2 1-nt         16098        0.472         0.547         0.371          0.470
# 3 2-nt         10781        0.383         0.409         0.324          0.380
# 4 3-nt         17316        0.352         0.361         0.293          0.324

# Calculate Spearman correlations and p-values in R
calculate_spearman <- function(df, predictor) {

  test <- cor.test(
    df$fitness_final,
    df[[predictor]],
    method = "spearman",
    exact = FALSE
  )

  tibble(
    n = nrow(df),
    spearman_rho = unname(test$estimate),
    p_value = test$p.value
  )
}

spearman_results <- correlation_data %>%
  group_by(genome_nt_mut_ham) %>%
  group_modify(~ bind_rows(
    calculate_spearman(.x, "evo2_7b_base") %>%
      mutate(model = "Evo2 (7B Base)"),

    calculate_spearman(.x, "evo2_7b_microviridae") %>%
      mutate(model = "Evo2 (7B Microviridae)")
  )) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(genome_nt_mut_ham, model, everything())

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: a reusable correlation bar plot function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_evo2_correlations <- function(
    data,
    correlation_method = "Spearman"
) {

  plot_data <- data %>%
    filter(method == correlation_method)

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = group,
      y = correlation,
      fill = model
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
      width = 0.65,
      color = NA
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", correlation)),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
      vjust = -0.5,
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        #"Evo2-7B Base" = "#496C89",
        #"Evo2-7B Microviridae" = "#B87963"
        
        #"Evo2-7B Base" = "#0068BA",
        "Evo2 (7B Base)" = "#0081D1",
        #"Evo2-7B Base" = "#F08160",
        "Evo2 (7B Microviridae)" = "#F1BB3E"
      )
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 0.65),
      breaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = paste0(correlation_method, " correlation"),
      fill = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        size = 11,
        color = "black"
      ),
      axis.text.y = element_text(
        color = "black"
      ),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "center",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12)
    )
}
```

```{r}
  !anyDuplicated(phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$gene_aa_mut_ID),

  all(is.finite(phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$evo2_base_orf)),
  all(is.finite(phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$evo2_micro_orf)),

  all(
    phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$n_nt_variants ==
      phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$n_1nt +
      phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$n_2nt +
      phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores$n_3nt
  )
)

cat("Unique 1AA Evo2 scores generated successfully.\n")
# Unique 1AA Evo2 scores generated successfully.


# Step 3. Merge with the experimental 1AA dataset
phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling_evo2 <-
  phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling %>%
  left_join(
    phix_evo2_orf_1aa_scores %>%
      select(
        gene_aa_mut_ID,
        n_nt_variants,
        n_1nt,
        n_2nt,
        n_3nt,
        evo2_base_orf,
        evo2_micro_orf,
        evo2_base_orf_sd,
        evo2_micro_orf_sd
      ),
    by = "gene_aa_mut_ID",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling_evo2) ==
    nrow(phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling)
)


# Step 4. Check coverage by protein
evo2_coverage_by_gene <-
  phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling_evo2 %>%
  group_by(aa_mut_gene) %>%
  summarise(
    n_experimental = n(),

    n_evo2_base = sum(!is.na(evo2_base_orf)),
    n_evo2_micro = sum(!is.na(evo2_micro_orf)),

    coverage_pct = 100 * n_evo2_base / n_experimental,

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(evo2_coverage_by_gene, n = Inf)

# Astar should have zero coverage, since we did not score it separately.


# Step 5. Calculate Spearman correlations
# For our initial benchmark, we can compare each Evo2 model against the measured amino-acid mutation effects.
evo2_correlations <-
  phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling_evo2 %>%
  filter(
    aa_mut_ham == 1,
    aa_mut_class == "Missense",
    !is.na(fitness_aa_mut),
    !is.na(evo2_base_orf),
    !is.na(evo2_micro_orf)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_mutations = n(),

    spearman_base = cor(
      fitness_aa_mut,
      evo2_base_orf,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    spearman_micro = cor(
      fitness_aa_mut,
      evo2_micro_orf,
      method = "spearman"
    )
  )

print(evo2_correlations)
# # A tibble: 1 × 3
#   n_mutations spearman_base spearman_micro
#         <int>         <dbl>          <dbl>
# 1       28381         0.314          0.263


# Step 6. Compare correlations across proteins
evo2_correlations_by_gene <-
  phix_proteome_dms_mut_Fitness_unique_modelling_evo2 %>%
  filter(
    aa_mut_ham == 1,
    aa_mut_class == "Missense",
    !is.na(fitness_aa_mut),
    !is.na(evo2_base_orf),
    !is.na(evo2_micro_orf)
  ) %>%
  group_by(aa_mut_gene) %>%
  summarise(
    n_mutations = n(),

    spearman_base = cor(
      fitness_aa_mut,
      evo2_base_orf,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    spearman_micro = cor(
      fitness_aa_mut,
      evo2_micro_orf,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(evo2_correlations_by_gene, n = Inf)

# ============================================================
# Convert Evo2 correlations to the existing format
# ============================================================

#library(dplyr)
#library(tidyr)

# 1) Convert the two Evo2 models into long format
evo2_performance_phix <- evo2_correlations_by_gene %>%
  filter(aa_mut_gene != "K") %>%
  select(
    aa_mut_gene,
    spearman_base,
    spearman_micro
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(spearman_base, spearman_micro),
    names_to = "model",
    values_to = "rho"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    predictor_name = case_when(
      model == "spearman_base" ~ "Evo2 (7B Base)",
      model == "spearman_micro" ~ "Evo2 (7B Microviridae)"
    ),

    gene_name = aa_mut_gene,
    predictor_target = gene_name,

    mean_rho = rho,
    median_rho = rho,

    sd_spearman_rho = NA_real_,
    n_datasets = 1L,

    predictor_input_modality = "DNA sequence",
    predictor_input_modality_simplified = "DNA Language Model (DLM)",

    predictor_rank_by_virus = NA_integer_,
    predictor_rank_average = NA_integer_
  ) %>%
  select(
    predictor_name,
    gene_name,
    predictor_target,
    mean_rho,
    median_rho,
    sd_spearman_rho,
    n_datasets,
    predictor_input_modality,
    predictor_rank_by_virus,
    predictor_rank_average,
    predictor_input_modality_simplified
  )

# QC
stopifnot(
  nrow(evo2_performance_phix) == 18,
  !anyDuplicated(
    evo2_performance_phix[
      c("predictor_name", "gene_name")
    ]
  )
)

print(evo2_performance_phix, n = Inf)


# 2) Bind Evo2 results to the previous performance table
predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind_evo2 <-
  predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind %>%
  bind_rows(
    evo2_performance_phix
  )

predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind_evo2 %>%
  filter(grepl("^Evo2", predictor_name)) %>%
  arrange(predictor_name, gene_name) %>%
  print(n = Inf)



# 3) Recalculate the overall predictor summary
# Clean combined ΦX174 performance table
phix_perf_clean_evo2 <-
  predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind_evo2 %>%
  filter(
    gene_name != "TEM-1 (Control)",
    gene_name != "K",
    !is.na(mean_rho),
    !is.na(median_rho)
  ) %>%
  select(
    gene_name,
    predictor_name,
    mean_rho,
    median_rho,
    predictor_input_modality,
    predictor_input_modality_simplified
  )

# Predictor metadata
predictor_metadata_evo2 <- phix_perf_clean_evo2 %>%
  select(
    predictor_name,
    predictor_input_modality,
    predictor_input_modality_simplified
  ) %>%
  distinct()

# Overall performance summary
phix_summary_overall_evo2 <- phix_perf_clean_evo2 %>%
  group_by(predictor_name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rho_phix = mean(mean_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rho_phix = median(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),

    sd_mean_rho_phix = sd(mean_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_median_rho_phix = sd(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),

    n_genes = n_distinct(gene_name),
    gene_names = paste(
      sort(unique(gene_name)),
      collapse = ", "
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    predictor_metadata_evo2,
    by = "predictor_name"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_rho_phix))

# Check where Evo2 ranks
phix_summary_overall_evo2 %>%
  mutate(
    rank = row_number()
  ) %>%
  filter(
    grepl("^Evo2", predictor_name)
  ) %>%
  print(width = Inf)

rsa_complex <- "RSA (complex)"

#evo2_micro_name <- "Evo2 7B Microviridae (ORF)"

# RSA monomer baseline
rsa_median_line_evo2 <- phix_perf_clean_evo2 %>%
  filter(predictor_name == rsa_monomer) %>%
  summarise(
    rsa_median = median(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%

stopifnot(

# Plot dataframe
phix_dot_plot_df_evo2 <- phix_perf_clean_evo2 %>%
  group_by(predictor_name) %>%
  mutate(
    predictor_median_rho = median(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_proteins = n_distinct(gene_name)
  ) %>%

  mutate(

phix_model_median_df_evo2 <- phix_dot_plot_df_evo2 %>%

y_max_evo2 <- max(phix_dot_plot_df_evo2$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE)

y_label_evo2 <- y_max_evo2 + 0.04
y_upper_evo2 <- y_max_evo2 + 0.12


# Number of available proteins
phix_n_label_df_evo2 <- phix_dot_plot_df_evo2 %>%

  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Spearman rho",
    title = "ΦX174 predictor performance by protein",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each dot is one protein; dashed line = median RSA (monomer), rho = ",
      round(rsa_median_line_evo2, 3)
    )
  )

# ============================================================
# Helper: extract gene-specific annotations from one slot
# ============================================================

extract_gene_annotations <- function(data, slot) {

  prefix <- if (slot == 1) {
    "gene_sub_aa_mut"
  } else {
    paste0("gene_sub_aa_mut", slot)
  }

  data %>%
    transmute(
      genome_mut_ID_nt,
      gene = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_gene")]],
      annotation_slot = slot,

      gene_aa_mut_ID = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_ID")]],
      gene_aa_mut_pos = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_pos")]],
      gene_aa_mut_wt = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_wt")]],
      gene_aa_mut_sub = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_sub")]],
      gene_aa_mut_class = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_class")]],
      gene_aa_mut_ham = .data[[paste0(prefix, "_ham")]],

      genome_nt_mut_ham,
      phix_aa_mut_ham
    ) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(gene),
      gene != ""
    )
}
```
